title: Learn ASP.NET Core Web API from the ground up
hook: ASP.NET Core is Microsoft's cross-platform framework for building production Web APIs on .NET. This track starts with how requests enter Kestrel and flow through middleware, then grows into the depth you need for senior interviews — DI lifetimes, JWT auth, EF Core performance, and observability.

blocks.text: .NET is a free, cross-platform developer platform. C# is the language; ASP.NET Core is the web framework for building HTTP APIs and services. You write endpoints in C#, register services in dependency injection (DI), and host the app with Kestrel — a high-performance web server. Unlike Node.js Express where you wire middleware manually, ASP.NET Core ships a built-in pipeline, configuration system, auth stack, and OpenAPI support. This track focuses on Web API fundamentals — not Razor Pages or MVC views.

sections.heading: How it differs from Node.js and Express

blocks.text: If you know Express or NestJS, ASP.NET Core will feel familiar — middleware, dependency injection, and route handlers — but the runtime model differs. Node.js runs on a single-threaded event loop; ASP.NET Core uses the thread pool with async/await for I/O. Express middleware is a function chain; ASP.NET Core middleware is a doubly-linked pipeline with explicit registration order. NestJS DI resembles ASP.NET Core's built-in container, but .NET enforces service lifetimes at runtime and throws on captive dependency mistakes.
